items.title: Pete Levin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: There was one European tour we did, the band was a little bigger than usual but the sax section was Dave Sanborn, Arthur Blythe, Steve Lacy and Howard Johnson and George Adams.

ctx.x: Oh that could take a whole other interview here. Well as an orchestrator his ideas, just the sounds and the textures that he envisioned were I think unique at the time when he first started doing it. And they made the sound of some bands that he was writing for, like Claude Thornhill and so forth, and when he applied that to specific projects, like some of his own ten, twelve piece groups, and then of course all the great stuff he did for Miles Davis, I mean just those sounds, the way he used instruments, the way…

I mean they just all think and play and perform with the same — it’s like one head. Sometimes somebody conducts, sometimes they don’t even bother. They just do it and the sax section blends so well. It’s just great. That’s the way you do a big band. Gil, it just never occurred to him. There was one European tour we did, the band was a little bigger than usual but the sax section was Dave Sanborn, Arthur Blythe, Steve Lacy and Howard Johnson and George Adams. Now these, Howard playing baritone sax — he plays it…

lot of Jimi Hendrix in Hiram’s playing. Not the exact notes or the riffs just the spirit that Hiram plays with. And Hiram does what he does and a lot of people didn’t like it. A lot of people didn’t like it. Audience. The band — we had a great time. And Hiram I remember him saying man, I don’t know what I’m doing in this band but I’m here. And Gil wrote for him, he featured him, he liked the way he played. And Delmar Brown was another one. Delmar is a wonderful player. He’s not real good at playing other people’s…
